## Requirements: run the browser E2E suite with file-level parallelism

The full browser suite currently runs with `workers: 1` and `fullyParallel: false`, so independent spec files execute one after another. Measured on the pinned ubuntu-24.04 image (2026-10-26), the full-suite `workflow_dispatch` takes 11m21s of job time (9m46s in `Run E2E tests`) for 34 file IDs / 267 tests, with 61% of the Playwright time in `terminal-consistency-faults.spec.ts` alone.

A source-identical two-worker run (same event, same image, same catalog, config change only) completes in 8m17s (6m16s in `Run E2E tests`) with **zero failed, skipped or flaky** tests — see #2205 for the evidence and the earlier ubuntu-26.04 arm. File-level parallelism therefore reduces PR feedback time without touching test semantics or the intentional 120s stalled-observer case.

This delivers only the worker-count change. It does not change required checks, does not add/remove E2E IDs, and does not split the dominant spec file (the next lever, tracked in #2205).

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 The exact PR head's selected E2E run executes the declared regression spec together with the coalesced browser-design IDs under `workers: 2` on the pinned ubuntu-24.04 image, with zero failed, skipped or flaky tests; the run's `Run E2E tests` step duration is recorded for the PR head (the workers=1 baseline comparison lives in #2205 evidence, not in this exact-head criterion).
